problem_statement: manuelernestog/astro-modern-personal-website is a runnable Astro + Tailwind + daisyUI static portfolio site, published here as “Meridian Lines” — a field journal of cartography and interface craft curated by Adaira Voss, with a lofi light palette (near-white #ffffff / #f7f7f8 panels, slate #0f172a ink, #e5e7eb hairline borders), a left sidebar nav (Home / Projects / Services / Store / Blog / CV / Contact) and rounded HorizontalCard blocks. The Projects page is the site’s Field Atlas of survey work but ships only unfilled starter cards. Design and ship the Field Atlas’s OWN discipline filter: a row of discipline tabs (All / Survey / Wayfinding / Cartography) derived from the six real survey projects’ disciplines that, when clicked, actually re-renders the survey cards to the matching discipline and updates a genuine result count (for example ‘Showing 2 of 6 · Wayfinding’). The Field Atlas summary (its ‘Selected surveys’ heading and count) is a shared companion that stays continuous across the site: it appears on the Projects page AND on the Home and Services pages, and the full filterable card grid renders on the Projects page. Keep the existing Meridian Lines identity — the near-white rounded panels with slate ink and hairline borders, the sidebar nav, the HorizontalCard language — so the filter reads as part of the same site, keeps its tab row and card grid within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, and emits no runtime console or network errors.
required_content: A real Field Atlas discipline filter (tabs All / Survey / Wayfinding / Cartography) sits above the survey card grid on the Projects page; clicking a discipline tab re-renders the cards to the matching discipline.
The control shows a genuine result count that re-derives from the active filter (e.g. 'Showing 6 of 6 · All disciplines' becomes 'Showing 2 of 6 · Wayfinding' when the Wayfinding tab is selected).

The Field Atlas summary (its 'Selected surveys' heading and count) is a shared companion that appears on the Projects page AND on the Home and Services pages (cross-page continuity); the full filterable card grid renders on the Projects page.

The filter tab row and the filtered card grid stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow and lay out cleanly (cards wrap into a single column rather than spilling, overlapping, or clipping).

The filter adopts the site's own near-white rounded panel, hairline border and slate accent, and the active tab is clearly legible (not near-white-on-near-white) — an on-brand atlas control, not a broken or illegible one.

The existing site stays intact: the Meridian Lines home hero, the featured surveys, the sidebar nav, the Blog and CV pages all continue to work alongside the new filter, and all captured states emit no runtime console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the site's visual language: the near-white #ffffff/#f7f7f8 panels, slate #0f172a ink, #e5e7eb hairline borders, rounded corners and sidebar nav; the filter and its cards must adopt this same identity.

Build the discipline tabs from the six survey projects' own disciplines (Survey / Wayfinding / Cartography), and render the shared Field Atlas summary companion so a single component rides the Projects, Home and Services surfaces rather than duplicating markup.

The filter tab row must wrap or shrink and stay within the mobile viewport at 390px, and the filtered card grid must reflow into a single column on narrow screens — do not pin the tabs to a fixed desktop width or force the cards into a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows a phone.

The result count and the visible card set must both re-derive from the live filter every render so they always match the selected tab; do not snapshot the grid or the count once and leave it stale when a tab is clicked.
Keep the filter visually part of the Projects page's Field Atlas rather than turning it into a separate banner or restyling the whole site; do not convert the site into a landing page or dashboard.
Do not introduce external fonts, analytics, stock imagery or remote requests; the filter reuses the site's own local assets and card language.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the Meridian Lines home hero at 1440px with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_initial captures the same home at 390px with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_projects scrolls to the Field Atlas filter and captures the discipline-tab row, the result count and the six survey cards (All filter) laid out cleanly in a rounded near-white panel.
mobile_projects scrolls to the same filter at 390px and captures the tab row and card grid reflowed within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_projects captures the filter at 834px where the tab row still fits, so no overflow is expected.
desktop_home_atlas captures the Home page; the shared Field Atlas summary companion must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_services captures the Services page; the shared Field Atlas summary companion must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_field_filter captures the Field Atlas after clicking the Wayfinding discipline tab: the grid re-filters to the two Wayfinding surveys and the count updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Wayfinding'.

change_completion: The Projects page has a working discipline-filter control (All / Survey / Wayfinding / Cartography).
Clicking a discipline tab re-renders the survey cards to that discipline and updates the result count to reflect it.
The site (home hero, featured surveys, sidebar nav, Blog, CV) remains intact alongside the filter.
The Projects, Home and Services pages stay reachable through the existing sidebar navigation.
design_consistency: The filter and cards adopt the site's near-white rounded panel, hairline border and slate accent, with a legible active tab.
The shared Field Atlas summary companion rides the Projects, Home and Services pages continuously (heading + count).
The rounded-card visual language and lofi typography are preserved across the filter and the existing pages.
regression: The 'Meridian Lines' home wordmark renders on the initial view.
The Field Atlas summary companion appears on the Home and Services pages, not only the Projects page, confirming cross-page continuity.
The featured surveys, the sidebar nav and the survey cards still render their content.
responsive: 390px mobile has no horizontal overflow; the discipline-tab row wraps/shrinks and stays within the viewport.
The filtered card grid reflows into a single column on mobile without spilling, overlapping, or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro + Tailwind + daisyUI portfolio task at L4 on manuelernestog/astro-modern-personal-website (astro-modern-personal-website, published as Meridian Lines), capability=Consistency, scope=cross_page. The graded change designs the site's OWN Field Atlas discipline filter on the Projects page: a discipline-tab control (All / Survey / Wayfinding / Cartography) built from six real survey project cards' disciplines that actually re-renders the cards and updates a real result count, with a shared 'Selected surveys' summary companion that rides the Projects, Home and Services pages. Four orthogonal machine-checked gates: no_horizontal_overflow on the 390px mobile views (the discipline-tab row must wrap, not pin to a fixed non-wrapping desktop width); visual_regression on the field-atlas component crops at desktop_projects + mobile_projects (an on-brand near-white #ffffff rounded panel with #e5e7eb hairline borders, slate #0f172a ink and a legible dark active tab and a clean two-column card grid, not a broken shingled overlapping pile of cards with a near-white-on-near-white illegible active tab); cross-page dom_assertions that the shared summary companion (fieldfilter--summary 'Selected surveys') rides the Home and Services pages as well as the Projects page; and interaction_assertions that clicking the Wayfinding discipline tab re-filters the grid and updates the count to 'Showing 2 of 6' (a snapshotted grid + count that never re-derives fails this). The baseline is the original layout defect (discipline-tab row pinned to a fixed 760px non-wrapping width, and the shared summary rendered on the Projects page only) which fails overflow + visual + cross-page but passes interaction; the known-bad 'smart wrong' filter keeps the narrow non-wrapping tab row, collapses the card grid into a heavily overlapping shingled pile with a near-white-on-near-white illegible active tab, is projects-only, and snapshots its grid and count at mount so the tab click succeeds but the terminal result stays stale, failing all four gates. INFRA fixes applied identically to all three legs (not part of the graded change): the @astrojs/sitemap integration is dropped from astro.config so the site builds cleanly offline, the starter-demo Projects and Services page copy is replaced with the six real Meridian Lines surveys and commissions, and the FieldSummary companion is wired into the Home and Services pages. The site's own local meridian-logo.svg and post_img.webp images and the HorizontalCard language are the design assets reused as-is.

Reassigned to this genuinely long-tail Astro repo from a duplicate of AlpayC/portfolio_site (owned by the lower-numbered slot_207).
